claim.text: QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 survives 500 m depth

note: Grounding strengthened (external review, item 12, re-checked 2026-10-24): originally rested on ONE QuSpin page's silence (https://quspin.com/qzfm-gen-3, actually a 2021 blog post, not the current product page); now independently re-checked across FOUR separate QuSpin-hosted pages -- the current product page (https://quspin.com/products-qzfm/), the original 2021 blog post, the mechanical dimensions page (https://quspin.com/qzfm-dimensions/), and the quick-start guide (https://quspin.com/products-qzfm/qzfm-quick-start-guide/) -- none states a pressure/depth/submersion/waterproofing/IP rating anywhere, and the product page explicitly frames the device as 'designed for magnetically shielded or actively field-controlled environments -- not direct operation in Earth's magnetic field,' consistent with a lab-only device nobody rates for submersion. Still no number to compare a claimed depth against, so this stays UNDETERMINED regardless of the depth asked about. Locks in the finding described in docs/extracted/constellation-robotics-seed.md §4; see also substrate.py's describe_gap(). (A fifth page, https://hse.ru/en/cdm-centre/brain/QZFM_Gen3, was checked and explicitly excluded as corroboration: it states its own text is copied verbatim from QuSpin, so it isn't an independent source.)
